ZONES.drinks: The cold cabinet on the back wall. Drinks are the shop’s magnet: everyone walks the length of the floor to reach them and passes everything else on the way.
ZONES.fresh: The open chiller on the west wall. Made today, gone tomorrow; open decks so a lunch can be taken without opening a door.
ZONES.pantry: The west gondola, beside the chiller: the cupboard at home, for people who cook.
ZONES.sweets: The middle gondola, on the door’s own line, so it is the first aisle you look down: crisps at a grown-up’s eye, children’s sweets low.
ZONES.daily: The east gondola, nearest the till: what runs out at home, heavy things low, small dear things where Thuan can see them.
ZONES.counter: On the counter by the register: hot, quick, and bought on impulse while paying.

tea.why: The everyday bottle: with lunch, on a hot walk, on the verandah.
tea.placed: First column, eye level: the drink most people come in for is the first one they see.

coffee.why: A sweet canned coffee before a dawn shift or between rounds.
coffee.placed: Under the tea, where a working hand reaches without looking.

water.why: Spring water for runs, patrols and long afternoons on the quay.
water.placed: Second column, eye level: the second most asked-for drink.

orange.why: Mandarin juice for a child’s lunch, or a breakfast in a hurry.
orange.placed: Low in the juice column, at a child’s reach.

cola.why: A cold cola after school or a shift.
cola.placed: Eye level in the third column: the impulse drink.

soda.why: Ramune with the marble: the summer drink children ask for by name.
soda.placed: Low under the cola, where children look.

milk.why: For the morning tea, the children, and the bathhouse fridge when it runs out.
milk.placed: Top of the last column: for people who knew what they came for.

beer.why: Umineko lager for the evening at home, the boat, or the walk to Minato.
beer.placed: The column nearest the till: beer is the last thing picked up, and Thuan sees who buys it.

rice.why: The lunch eaten standing up: plum onigiri, made this afternoon.
rice.placed: Eye level in the chiller: the shop’s best seller where nobody has to look for it.

bento.why: A proper lunch for people who cannot leave their work: the power house, the workshop, the office.
bento.placed: Under the rice balls: the dearer lunch beside the cheap one.

sandwich.why: Egg sandwiches eaten at a desk or on the ferry.
sandwich.placed: Middle bay, eye level, over the bread it is made from.

bread.placed: Under the sandwiches: the household buy below the snack.

pudding.why: A small treat: after homework, after a long shelf, after the bath.
pudding.placed: Top deck of the last bay: the treat at eye level, where it is hard to walk past.

yogurt.why: Plain yoghurt for a light breakfast and a careful stomach.
yogurt.placed: Under the pudding, for the people with good intentions.

noodles.why: Cup noodles for a late night or a typhoon day indoors.
noodles.placed: Pantry, front face: quick food first.

soup.why: Miso sachets for one bowl when cooking a pot is too much.
soup.placed: Beside the noodles: the other thing you add hot water to.

curry.why: Curry roux for a family dinner; Mrs Sato swears it is not for the shop.
curry.placed: Pantry, front face, low: a heavy box for a cook who comes back every week.

soy.why: Soy sauce for a kitchen that ran out mid-service.
soy.placed: Pantry, back face: the staple, found by people who already know where it is.

tuna.why: Tinned tuna for onigiri at home and for the cat that is not officially fed.
tuna.placed: Back face, with the other tins.

peaches.why: Tinned peaches for visiting someone who is ill, as one does.
peaches.placed: Back face, high: an occasional buy, not in the way.

chips.why: Salted crisps with a beer or a baseball game on the radio.
chips.placed: Front face at a grown-up’s eye, seen on the way back from the beer.

crackers.why: Soy rice crackers with tea, for visitors.
crackers.placed: Front face, the low boards: a big bag for visitors, easy to lift down, under the crisps.

biscuit.why: Butter biscuits for a reading afternoon or a night at the press.
biscuit.placed: Front face, top: the gift-sized packet where it can be seen.

chocolate.placed: Back face, low: at a child’s eye, below a parent’s.

candy.why: Fruit sweets, the ten-yen kind of treat.
candy.placed: The lowest shelf of the back face, where small hands find it first.

detergent.why: Laundry powder: the bathhouse towels and a family’s week.
detergent.placed: Bottom of the front face: the heaviest thing in the shop, low and near the door out.

soap.why: Sakura soap for the bath and the shop’s own washroom.
soap.placed: Above the detergent: washing beside washing.

tissues.why: Tissues for hay fever, a cold, or a sad film.
tissues.placed: Front face, next bay: bulky and light, at hand height.

toothpaste.why: Mint toothpaste, the thing you notice has run out at night.
toothpaste.placed: Above the tissues, with the bathroom.

battery.why: Dry cells for radios, torches and the harbour lamp.
battery.placed: Back face, nearest the till: small, dear and easy to pocket, so Thuan can see them.

notebook.why: Pocket notebooks for tide times, articles and homework.
notebook.placed: Beside the batteries: stationery with the small things.

postcard.why: Harbour postcards for visitors and for letters to the main island.
postcard.placed: Back face, by the till, beside the stamps Thuan sells.

bun.why: A steamed pork bun to eat walking out of the door.
bun.placed: In the steamer on the counter: smelt while paying, bought on impulse.

sakura.name: Sakura Shōten (Sakura Trading)
sakura.goods: Everyday goods: drinks, food, washing, paper goods, batteries.

higa-saketen.name: Higa Liquor
stock: awamori, from the 180 ml bottles to the clay kame

rainflower-florist.name: Rainflower Florist
rainflower-florist.goods: Flowers and decorations: the season’s window dressing, festival trimmings, wreaths.

frontrow.name: Front-Row Books & Stationery
stock: A4 copy paper by the ream

izakaya.name: Minato Izakaya
izakaya.why: Soy for the grill, water for chasers, mandarin juice for the shōchū mixes, table tissues, cloth washing, and batteries for the karaoke microphone.
izakaya.delivery: Two crates on the trolley at three, before the noren goes up; Thao signs for it.

ramen.name: Sato Ramen
ramen.why: Soy to top up the tare, tea for the counter, and powder for the towels.
ramen.delivery: At half past ten, while the stock comes up to the boil.

onsen.name: Umi-no-yu
onsen.why: Bottled milk and ramune for the fridge by the bandai — the after-bath drink — soap for the washing stools, and powder for the towels.
onsen.delivery: Mornings before the bath opens; the milk crate is the heaviest thing Thuan carries all week.

frontrow.name: Front-Row Books & Stationery
frontrow.why: Tea and biscuits for the reading corner, batteries for the press-room radio.
frontrow.delivery: Thursdays, when the evening paper is set and there is a quiet hour.

form3d.name: Chin & Tetsuo Repairs
form3d.why: Batteries by the box for testing radios, canned coffee for the bench, and a lunch order of rice balls.
form3d.delivery: Lunch at noon on the bicycle; batteries when Tetsuo remembers to ask.

office.name: Johansson Harbour Office
office.why: Batteries for the quay lamps, and drinks for the crews.
office.delivery: With the first ferry, on the harbour cart.

koban.name: Minato Police Box
koban.why: Water and a rice ball for the night patrol, batteries for the torch.
koban.delivery: Officer Mori collects it himself, at closing, and calls it a patrol.

mayor-office.name: the mayor’s office
mayor-office.why: Tea and rice crackers for visitors, and tissues for difficult meetings.
mayor-office.delivery: Mondays, carried up the Community Hall stairs.

community-kitchen.name: the community kitchen
community-kitchen.why: The Saturday curry for the whole street, and onigiri for the volunteers.
community-kitchen.delivery: Friday evening, so the pot can start early.

school.name: the island school
school.why: School milk, and tissues every hay-fever season.
school.delivery: First thing on Mondays, by the school gate.

clinic.name: the clinic
clinic.why: Tissues and soap for the waiting room, water for patients, and tinned peaches for anyone kept in overnight.
clinic.delivery: Whenever the clinic telephones; it is never urgent and always is.

market.name: Sakura Shōten
market.why: The beer column in Sakura’s cold cabinet, nearest the till.
market.delivery: Saturday mornings: the Higas’ van, and Grandmother Higa counting the cases off herself.

izakaya.name: Minato Izakaya
izakaya.why: Everything behind Minato’s bar: the tap, the keep shelf, the tokkuri and the highballs.
izakaya.delivery: Kegs on Tuesdays and Fridays at two, rolled down the side passage before the noren goes up.

ramen.name: Sato Ramen
ramen.why: A bottle with the gyōza, for the lunch crowd who are not going back to work.
ramen.delivery: With the Minato order, one crate left at the back door.

fujita-shed.name: Mr Fujita’s shed on the pier
fujita-shed.why: Twenty-four to forty-nine large bottles a day, three small glasses a bottle, poured from the armchair in front of the television.
fujita-shed.delivery: Six every morning at the pier root: the day’s crates down, yesterday’s empties up off his floor. Returnable bottles, counted by Grandmother Higa.

market.name: Sakura Shōten
market.why: Sakura’s windows follow the town calendar: the season’s dressing goes up the week before every festival.
market.delivery: The Sunday before each festival, after closing; Mrs Kinjō dresses the window herself.

izakaya.name: Minato Izakaya
lines: a vase of flowers for the counter
izakaya.why: Fresh lanterns when the old ones fade, and one stem on the counter that Thao pretends not to care about.
izakaya.delivery: Flowers on Mondays; lanterns when the typhoon has had the last ones.

mayor-office.name: the mayor’s office
lines: a garland for the Merry Moose
mayor-office.why: Openings, prize days and the town’s festivals, and the moose is dressed for every one of them.
mayor-office.delivery: The morning of each ceremony, carried up the Community Hall stairs.

onsen.name: Umi-no-yu
onsen.why: A small vase on the bandai, changed with the season, the first thing a bather sees.
onsen.delivery: Every other Saturday, before the bath opens.

school.name: the island school
school.why: Sports day in the autumn and the graduation in March.
school.delivery: The day before, with the children helping to carry.

office.name: Johansson Harbour Office
lines: log books for tides and freight
office.why: The harbour’s records: tide tables, freight manifests and receipts for the ferry.
office.delivery: Reiko drops it off on her way to the evening press.

mayor-office.name: the mayor’s office
mayor-office.why: Minutes, letters to the main island, the town accounts and the notice board.

school.name: the island school
school.why: A new term’s exercise books, and the glue that is always running out.
school.delivery: The week before term, in boxes the children carry in.

koban.name: Minato Police Box
koban.why: The incident book has to be the right kind, and pens disappear from a police box.

market.name: Sakura Shōten
market.why: The till’s receipt rolls, Sakura’s own trade ledgers, and labels for the price gun.

SAKURA_DRESSING.title: Look over the delivery shelf
SAKURA_DRESSING.text: Cartons off the morning van, waiting to be priced up and put out. Thuan works down them after closing.

SAKURA_DRESSING.title: Read the end-cap promotion
SAKURA_DRESSING.text: Hinode Curry Roux — the month’s offer, stacked at the end of the aisle with a hand-lettered card.

SAKURA_DRESSING.title: Read the ramen-week card
SAKURA_DRESSING.text: Ramen week: any two YUNAGI cups for ¥280. Thuan has written underneath, in smaller letters, that the kettle by the till is for customers.

SAKURA_DRESSING.title: Read the new-release card
SAKURA_DRESSING.text: New: KOGANE lightly salted. Jaga-bō on the bag, Jaga-bō on the card, Jaga-bō by the window. The rep is very proud of him.
